meta.caveat: MIT SuperCloud publishes this as a four-month sample of the cluster's jobs and says it is not appropriate for estimating system utilization. Every figure describes the sample. The storage incident (pvc/scratch-lustre-02) is synthetic; everything else is computed from real telemetry.

provenance.caveat: SM utilization is a proxy for useful work. A data-loader-bound or communication-bound job does real work at low SM occupancy. Anchored at ALLOCATED, not purchased — this release is a job sample, so a purchased-capacity denominator is not defensible.

actions.title: End allocations that sit at zero
actions.action: Kill a job whose GPUs have shown 0% for an hour. 15,070 jobs held cards for a median of 96 hours without ever running a single kernel.
actions.owner: Scheduler policy (SRE on-call owns the timeout)
actions.risk: A job slow to start -- staging data, a long CPU preamble -- gets killed before it computes. Within this data a peak of exactly 0% means no kernel ever ran, so there are no false positives here; the exposure is future jobs that behave differently.
actions.evidence_note: jobs.parquet: sm_util_avg = 0 AND sm_util_max = 0 AND state != COMPLETED; hours returned = gpu_hours x (walltime - grace) / walltime

actions.title: Send CPU work to CPU nodes
actions.action: Default the map-reduce and batch launchers to no GPU. Two thirds of LLMapReduce GPU time never opened the GPU at all -- no kernel, no GPU memory, idle power draw.
actions.owner: Research computing (launcher defaults) + the 10 owners below
actions.risk: A job that crashed before reaching its GPU code looks identical. Offload only jobs that completed, or owners whose jobs are consistently like this. A wrong move is cheap: the job fails fast or runs slow and its owner resubmits with a GPU.
actions.evidence_note: jobs.parquet: sm_util_max = 0 AND max_gpu_mem_used = 0; median watts_avg 25.8 = an idle V100. Requests fit a 40-core/384 GiB node for 97% of these hours.

actions.title: Right-size two-GPU requests that use one card
actions.action: 689 jobs held a second card that never worked while the first one did. Invisible in the job table, which averages the cards.
actions.risk: A multi-GPU job cancelled or crashed before its parallel phase looks the same. 4,753 of these GPU-hours are on cancelled jobs. Act only where an owner's pattern repeats on jobs that completed.
actions.evidence_note: gpus.parquet pivoted per gpu_id: busiest card >= 20% SM, quietest < 5%, per-card hours clipped to the job's walltime. In 885 of 943 two-card jobs the idle card is card 0, which holds a 0.44 GiB framework context.

recoverable.basis: Jobs that never ran a kernel (returned by an idle timeout or moved to CPU), half of near-idle jobs, half of idle second cards. CANCELLED is not counted as waste in itself -- only the idle time before the cancel.

wrong.title: Drain the 5 machines with the most findings
wrong.cost_note: 21,840 GPU-hours of capacity removed over a 13-week quarter, and the failing scripts would fail on whatever machine they land on next.
wrong.why: The ranking counts findings per machine and never reads rootCauses. 664 of those findings resolve to failing Slurm arrays, not to the machines. Case 6 triage finds no hardware on any of the five. The one machine that really did break ranks 21st.

causal.root_cause: array/65192801012 — 22 of 22 tasks failed, 100% with exit code 256, spread across 10 machines (median runtime 2055s)

wrong.title: Drain the 121 machines in the storage incident
wrong.cost_note: 11,616 GPU-hours over 48 hours -- 54% of the cluster -- and every machine comes back to the same volume.
wrong.why: POST /v1/causal on any one of the 121 findings resolves them all to one shared volume, pvc/scratch-lustre-02, at score 0.88. One ticket to the storage team, not 121 drains. The findings' own degraded hours are exactly the GPU-hours those machines ran in the 48 h before detection, which we reproduced from gpus.parquet (correlation 1.000).

causal.root_cause: pvc/scratch-lustre-02 degraded — filesystem p99 latency rose 30.3x, affecting 121 nodes

wrong.title: Count every cancelled job as waste
wrong.cost_note: 116,692 GPU-hours of cancelled work was computing when it was stopped. Promising that as a saving is promising work that was already useful.
wrong.why: Cancelled jobs ran at 34.3% hour-weighted utilization against the cluster's 38.5%. A cancellation is usually a researcher correctly killing a bad run. The waste is the idle time before the cancel, which the idle-timeout action already counts.

wrong.title: Price queue waiting as engineer salary
wrong.chart_note: kept out of the chart beside the others: this one is a number to correct, not capacity to destroy
wrong.cost_note: Counted per person and only past a 4-hour target, waiting is 3,719 person-hours (46 people, about 4.5 h each per week) -- an upper bound of $353K, not $9.3M.
wrong.why: The endpoint multiplies every job's wait_sec by $95. 53% of jobs are array tasks, so one person waiting on 1,000 tasks is counted 1,000 times; 23% of the hours are jobs held by their own dependencies, not queueing; and rules::queue-starvation's own text says this is elapsed time, not staffed time. Interactive sessions -- a person at a keyboard -- waited 0.8 hours in four months.
